note: PROPOSED answers, pending the owner's review. Confidence = how many of three independent lenses named the same requirement. Foundry columns are corroboration only, never a source of values.

rows.name: Branched Tree Of Pain
rows.text: **Usage** imbued into a weapon ikon that deals piercing or slashing damage --- The blade of your ikon takes one or more notches, capable of dealing mortal pain to your foes. **Immanence** When you Strike with the ikon, you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success. This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure. **Transcendence—Plant Thirty Barbs** ⟨1⟩ (death, transcendence)

proposed.clause: **Transcendence—Plant Thirty Barbs** ⟨1⟩ (death, transcendence)
proposed.freeText: The character gains a named single-action activity, Plant Thirty Barbs, with the death and transcendence traits; it must appear as an action the player can find and use.

proposed.clause: **Immanence** When you Strike with the ikon, you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success.
proposed.freeText: An immanence state for this ikon that the player can turn on and off — the benefit only runs while the exemplar's spark rests in this ikon, so the sheet needs a switchable state rather than a permanent entry.

proposed.clause: you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success. This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure.
proposed.freeText: While immanence is on, Strikes made with the weapon this ikon is imbued into crit on a natural 19, but only when that 19 would already be a success. This is an expanded critical range on YOUR OWN Strike — no lane expresses critical-range changes, so at minimum that specific Strike needs a marker carrying the rule where the player rolls it.

proposed.clause: **Usage** imbued into a weapon ikon that deals piercing or slashing damage
proposed.freeText: The player must designate which owned weapon this ikon is imbued into, restricted to weapons that deal piercing or slashing damage. Every later clause reads "the ikon", so the sheet cannot resolve them without that stored pick.

proposed.clause: you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success. This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure.
proposed.freeText: An expanded critical range on Strikes with the imbued weapon — a natural 19 crits when 19 would otherwise be a success. This is not a bonus to attack, damage, or a DC, so nothing numeric can carry it; it has to print on the strike itself while the ikon's state is on.

proposed.clause: **Usage** imbued into a weapon ikon that deals piercing or slashing damage
proposed.freeText: The sheet must let the player bind this record to ONE specific owned weapon (only ones dealing piercing or slashing qualify) and route everything below to that weapon's Strikes alone rather than to all Strikes. A per-record item binding — the record is inert until the player names which weapon it lives in.

proposed.clause: **Immanence** When you Strike with the ikon, you critically succeed if you roll a 19 on the die as long as that result would be a success. This has no effect on a 19 if the result would be a failure.
proposed.freeText: An altered critical threshold: a natural 19 that would already be a success becomes a critical success — but only on Strikes with the bound weapon, only while the ikon's immanence is active, and explicitly NOT when the 19 would be a failure. This is a change to how the die result is read, not a modifier, so nothing in a bonus or trait field can express it.

rows.name: Hydraulic Maneuvers
rows.text: You batter your foes with a torrent of water siphoned from your surroundings. If the next action you take is an Athletics check to Disarm, Shove, or Trip, that action has a range of 15 feet. You don't receive any item bonuses to that check or any circumstance bonuses related to your physical body, but if you roll a critical failure on that Athletics check, you get a failure instead.

proposed.clause: You don't receive any item bonuses to that check or any circumstance bonuses related to your physical body, but if you roll a critical failure on that Athletics check, you get a failure instead.
proposed.freeText: Must be able to say that this one Athletics check drops every item bonus and any circumstance bonus that comes from your body, and that a critical failure on it becomes a failure. Both land on your OWN roll — a bonus suppression and a degree-of-success upgrade — and no lane covers either, so the printed clause has to travel with the action to where Athletics is rolled.

proposed.clause: If the next action you take is an Athletics check to Disarm, Shove, or Trip, that action has a range of 15 feet.
proposed.freeText: The character must have this as a usable named activity on the sheet. Granting the following Disarm/Shove/Trip a 15-foot range is the activity's own resolution — the player performs it — so it needs no separate stat surface beyond the action being present with its text.

proposed.clause: You batter your foes with a torrent of water siphoned from your surroundings. If the next action you take is an Athletics check to Disarm, Shove, or Trip, that action has a range of 15 feet...
proposed.freeText: The character gains this as a usable named activity on the sheet, with its full text reachable — the range change, the bonus suppression, and the crit-fail-becomes-fail clause are read off that text when the player performs it.

proposed.clause: If the next action you take is an Athletics check to Disarm, Shove, or Trip, that action has a range of 15 feet.
proposed.freeText: A marker on the Disarm, Shove and Trip actions (and on Athletics) saying they are performed at a 15-foot range in this window. The reach/range at which a maneuver can be attempted is not a number the sheet totals anywhere, so it can only be printed against the actions it changes.

proposed.clause: but if you roll a critical failure on that Athletics check, you get a failure instead
proposed.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade — critical failure becomes failure — scoped to one named check. It moves the outcome band, not the modifier.

rows.name: Zombie Dedication
rows.text: Despite your death and subsequent reanimation as a rotting corpse, you retain most of your mind and identity. Yet, it's always there: the hunger for the flesh and organs of the living. You gain the undead and zombie traits, and the basic undead benefits. Unlike a typical zombie, you're not mindless. Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet. Your fist loses the nonlethal trait. Because of its progressing state of decay, your body requires continual maintenance to remain at its best. Each day after your rest period, your body is due to natural decay. Additionally, some zombie abilities allow you to push for a greater effect in exchange for a chance of deteriorating your body. While your body is deteriorated, you're Slowed 1. You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations. Because it's a natural result of your body's functions, you can't remove the slowed condition from deterioration through any other means. You crave the flesh of the living. You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage. Your jaws are in the brawling group and have the unarmed trait. You can use your jaws Strike only against a creature that's grabbed or restrained by you.

proposed.clause: You gain the undead and zombie traits
proposed.freeText: The character picks up the undead and zombie creature traits, which change what can target and affect them (undead-only effects, and everything keyed to being undead). No lane grants a creature trait to the character.

proposed.clause: Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet.
proposed.freeText: A permanent -5 feet applied to every Speed the character has, not just the land Speed.

proposed.clause: While your body is deteriorated, you're Slowed 1. You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations.
proposed.freeText: A deteriorated state the player can switch on and off, showing Slowed 1 while it is on, and cleared only by the 10-minute repair (which can ride along with daily preparations) — the text explicitly blocks removing that slowed by any other means.

proposed.clause: Your fist loses the nonlethal trait.
proposed.freeText: The character's existing fist unarmed Strike must have the nonlethal trait removed from its trait list — an edit to a strike the character already had, not a new one.

proposed.clause: You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage. Your jaws are in the brawling group and have the unarmed trait.
proposed.freeText: A new jaws unarmed Strike on the strikes list: 1d8 piercing, brawling weapon group, unarmed trait, rolled with the character's own attack bonus and damage modifiers.

proposed.clause: You can use your jaws Strike only against a creature that's grabbed or restrained by you.
proposed.freeText: The jaws Strike carries a usage restriction — legal only against a creature you have grabbed or restrained — and that restriction has to print with the strike itself, since nothing about the strike's numbers changes.

proposed.clause: and the basic undead benefits
proposed.freeText: The whole basic undead benefits package must reach the sheet: the standing immunities it confers (death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison, sleep, unconscious) and void healing — void damage heals you while vitality damage harms you. The immunities have a lane; the healing reversal does not.

proposed.clause: You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations.
proposed.freeText: A daily-preparation decision — spend the 10 minutes to clear the deteriorated state, or start the day slowed. The clause that nothing else can remove that slowed condition means this repair is the only thing allowed to clear the state.

proposed.clause: You gain … the basic undead benefits.
proposed.freeText: 'Basic undead benefits' is a reference to a rules package, not a mechanic in itself; the sheet must expand it into its parts. The immunity portion: immune to death effects, disease, paralyzed, poison and sleep, plus no need to breathe, eat, drink, or sleep.

proposed.clause: You gain … the basic undead benefits.
proposed.freeText: The same referenced package grants darkvision.

proposed.clause: You gain … the basic undead benefits.
proposed.freeText: The same package grants negative healing — void energy restores your Hit Points and vitality energy damages you. That is an inversion of which damage type heals versus harms, a rule about the character's relationship to two energy types; nothing expresses a flipped healing polarity (it is not a resistance, an immunity, or a weakness).

proposed.clause: Each day after your rest period, your body is due to natural decay. … You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations.
proposed.freeText: The deteriorated state re-arms itself every day after rest, and clearing it is a 10-minute repair that can be folded into daily preparations. This is a recurring daily upkeep step with a duration attached, not a choice among options — nothing is being picked, a state is being reset.

rows.name: Ascended Celestial Dedication
rows.text: Your Calling has driven you to perform mortal deeds that will result in your ascension to the ranks of celestials. You're headstrong and determined and hardly waver in your resolve; once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw. If you ever become confused, rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends. Additionally, you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait. As long as your nimbus is active, all allies in the area of your nimbus gain a +1 status bonus to saves against fear. You gain the Bless Ally action.

proposed.clause: If you ever become confused, rather than attack wildly, you become stubbornly immobile, wasting all your actions until the condition ends.
proposed.freeText: The Confused condition resolves differently for this character — no wild attacks, instead immobile and losing all actions for the duration — so the marker belongs on the Confused condition itself, the same shape as a Dying-condition marker.

proposed.clause: You gain the Bless Ally action.
proposed.freeText: A named action, Bless Ally, must appear on the sheet as something the character can use.

proposed.clause: once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw
proposed.freeText: A once-per-hour use the player can spend and see refresh. Spending it makes you roll a Will save twice and keep the higher — a fortune effect, not a bonus, so the Will save also needs a marker saying it is available. The use pool has a lane; the reroll itself has none.

proposed.clause: you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait.
proposed.freeText: A toggle the player flips with a single concentrate action, starting on. It moves none of the character's own numbers, so a display-only state showing whether the nimbus is currently lit is all it has to be.

proposed.clause: Additionally, you emanate a nimbus of light. You shed bright light in a 30-foot radius (and dim light to the next 30 feet). You can suppress or reestablish this light as a single action that has the concentrate trait.
proposed.freeText: A state recording whether the nimbus is currently shining, which the player can suppress and reestablish (a single concentrate action). It moves none of your own numbers — display-only — but it must be switchable because the rest of the feat is worded 'as long as your nimbus is active'.

proposed.clause: you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw
proposed.freeText: A fortune effect marked on Will saves: roll twice, keep the higher. It is not a numeric bonus, so it has to sit as a marker on the Will save with its once-per-hour cost stated.

proposed.clause: once per hour, you can roll twice and use the higher result on a Will saving throw
proposed.freeText: A fortune effect on Will saves — roll the d20 twice and keep the higher — together with the per-hour use tracker that limits it. Rolling twice changes how the roll is made rather than what is added to it, so no bonus field expresses it; and the limit is per HOUR, a period shorter than a day.

rows.name: Adroit Manipulation
rows.text: **Access** Mihrini ethnicity --- You've fiddled with knots, locks, and blacksmith's puzzles since you were a child to give your hands something to do. You gain the trained proficiency rank in Thievery (or another skill of your choice, if you're already trained in Thievery). If you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead.

proposed.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Thievery
proposed.freeText: Trained proficiency in Thievery, folded into the Thievery modifier on the sheet.

proposed.clause: (or another skill of your choice, if you're already trained in Thievery)
proposed.freeText: If the character is already trained in Thievery, the grant must instead become a free pick of any other skill — the player chooses and the sheet records which, so the training is never wasted.

proposed.clause: If you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead.
proposed.freeText: A success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock counts as a critical success. It is a degree-of-success upgrade on your own roll with no number attached, so it has to print against Thievery / the Pick a Lock action where the player will be rolling.

proposed.clause: If you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead.
proposed.freeText: A degree-of-success step-up, not a bonus: on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, success becomes critical success. It marks Thievery (the only skill that performs Pick a Lock) with the trigger printed, since no numeric value exists to add.

proposed.clause: If you roll a success on a Thievery check to Pick a Lock, you get a critical success instead.
proposed.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade — success becomes critical success — bound to one specific skill ACTION (Pick a Lock), not to Thievery generally. It changes the outcome band, so it cannot be a modifier; it has to mark the Pick a Lock action and be visible from Thievery.

rows.name: Adhyabhau
rows.text: You descend from the rare psychic vampires known as vetalaranas. Your forebear gained sustenance from the mental and emotional energy of living creatures, which manifests in you as powerful resistance to such effects. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait, and when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead.

proposed.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait
proposed.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus that applies only to Will saves against effects with the emotion trait. Because the rules restrict it, it belongs as a conditional entry carrying 'against emotion effects' rather than inside the flat Will save total.

proposed.clause: when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead
proposed.freeText: A success on ANY saving throw — not just Will — against an emotion effect becomes a critical success. A degree-of-success upgrade on your own save with no lane to compute it, so it must print against the saves alongside the +1, with its wider scope made clear.

proposed.clause: and when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead
proposed.freeText: A degree-of-success step-up on ANY saving throw against an emotion effect (wider than the +1, which is Will-only): success becomes critical success. No number to add, so it has to print as a marker on the saves with its trigger.

proposed.clause: when you roll a success on a saving throw against such an effect, you get a critical success instead
proposed.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade — success becomes critical success — on ANY saving throw against an emotion effect, not just Will. It shifts the outcome band rather than the modifier, and its scope is deliberately wider than the bonus in the previous clause, so it cannot simply ride along with that entry.

rows.name: Eternal Blessing
rows.text: Your deeds have brought your deity's grace to you for all of eternity. You're continuously surrounded by a Bless spell, with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up). The radius is 15 feet, and you can't increase it. You can Dismiss the spell; if you do, it returns automatically after 1 minute.

proposed.clause: You can Dismiss the spell; if you do, it returns automatically after 1 minute.
proposed.freeText: The blessing must be switchable off and back on, so the +1 status attack bonus can be suppressed while it is dismissed.

proposed.clause: You're continuously surrounded by a Bless spell.
proposed.freeText: Your own attack rolls must carry a permanent +1 status bonus. The emanation originates on you, so you are always within it — this is the decided aura shape: a permanent star on attack rolls with the positional wording in the note. The bonus allies get is not your sheet's business.

proposed.clause: with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up). The radius is 15 feet, and you can't increase it.
proposed.freeText: The effect's spell rank must be shown as scaling with level (half your level rounded up). It moves no number of yours — Bless's only heightening is radius and this feat fixes the radius — so it needs printing only (it matters for counteracting).

proposed.clause: You're continuously surrounded by a Bless spell
proposed.freeText: A permanently active, self-affecting instance of a spell the feat never restates. Because you are always at the centre of your own emanation, Bless's +1 status bonus to attack rolls applies to you unconditionally — so the sheet must carry a flat status bonus to ATTACK ROLLS whose value and type live in a different record. No lane in the vocabulary covers a flat attack-roll bonus, and none covers 'you permanently have spell X running on you' as a state rather than as a castable.

proposed.clause: with a spell rank equal to half your level (rounded up)
proposed.freeText: The rank of that continuous effect is a formula on character level (ceil(level/2)), not a fixed number. Granted-spell surfaces store a rank as a literal; this one has to be stored as a level-derived expression and re-derived every time the character levels.

proposed.clause: The radius is 15 feet, and you can't increase it
proposed.freeText: Prints the fixed 15-foot emanation, and — the mechanical part — suppresses the referenced spell's own area growth (Bless's Sustain/heightening increase). That is an override of a parameter on a record this feat itself supplies, so the note has to be attached to the granted effect rather than to the feat in isolation.

rows.name: Twitchy
rows.text: You are naturally suspicious and wary of danger, especially when you suspect someone might be leading you into an ambush. You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC and saves against hazards, and to all of your initiative rolls. If at least one of your opponents is using Deception or Diplomacy to determine their initiative, your bonus to initiative from this feat increases to +4.

proposed.clause: You gain a +1 circumstance bonus to AC ... against hazards.
proposed.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus to AC that applies only against hazards — restricted, so it sits outside the AC total with 'against hazards' as its condition.

proposed.clause: ...and to all of your initiative rolls.
proposed.freeText: A +1 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls, whatever statistic is being rolled for initiative (Perception, Stealth, Deception, a Lore, etc.) — it must attach to the initiative roll itself, not to one skill.

proposed.clause: If at least one of your opponents is using Deception or Diplomacy to determine their initiative, your bonus to initiative from this feat increases to +4.
proposed.freeText: An upgraded value: +4 circumstance to initiative under the stated condition, replacing the +1 entry rather than stacking with it. The trigger is enemy-side knowledge the player supplies, but the number that changes is yours.

rows.name: Natural Ambition
rows.text: You were raised to be ambitious and always reach for the stars, leading you to progress quickly in your chosen field. You gain a 1st-level class feat for your class. You must meet the prerequisites, but you can select the feat later in the character creation process in order to determine which prerequisites you meet.

proposed.clause: You gain a 1st-level class feat for your class.
proposed.freeText: An extra pick of one class feat of level 1 or lower, restricted to your own class's feat list, held separately from your normal class-feat slots.

proposed.clause: You must meet the prerequisites, but you can select the feat later in the character creation process in order to determine which prerequisites you meet.
proposed.freeText: Changes when the granted pick's prerequisites are evaluated: against the finished character, not against the build as it stood when the pick was offered. The sheet must tolerate this pick sitting unfilled, and must validate its prerequisites late without reporting the character as illegal in the interim.

rows.name: Divine Health
rows.text: Your faith makes you resistant to disease, protecting you as you offer succor to the ill. You gain a +2 status bonus to saves against diseases and poisons and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage. Allies in your champion's aura get this benefit, but their bonus is +1. In addition, if you roll a success on a save against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead. (Your allies don't share this benefit.) If you have the Sacred Body class feature, when you roll a critical failure on a save against a disease or poison, you get a failure instead.

proposed.clause: You gain a +2 status bonus to saves against diseases and poisons.
proposed.freeText: A +2 status bonus to saving throws restricted to disease and poison effects — outside the save totals, with the restriction stated.

proposed.clause: ...and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage.
proposed.freeText: A +2 status bonus to the flat check that ends persistent poison damage. It has no stat row of its own, so it must attach to the thing it modifies — the persistent-damage recovery check — with the value inline.

proposed.clause: If you have the Sacred Body class feature, when you roll a critical failure on a save against a disease or poison, you get a failure instead.
proposed.freeText: A second degree-of-success change on the same saves — critical failure becomes failure — that only exists if the character also has the Sacred Body class feature, so the sheet must gate it on possessing that feature.

proposed.clause: if you roll a success on a save against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead.
proposed.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade (success becomes critical success) on saves against disease and poison. Not computable by the sheet, so it must be printed alongside the same disease/poison save surface as the +2.

proposed.clause: If you have the Sacred Body class feature, when you roll a critical failure on a save against a disease or poison, you get a failure instead.
proposed.freeText: A second degree-of-success upgrade (critical failure becomes failure) on the same saves, which must appear only when the character actually has the Sacred Body class feature.

proposed.clause: if you roll a success on a save against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead
proposed.freeText: The sheet must be able to say that this character's degree of success on disease and poison saves is upgraded one step from success to critical success — an outcome-step change on a named category of save, not a numeric modifier.

proposed.clause: and to flat checks to recover from persistent poison damage
proposed.freeText: A flat check is not a statistic on the sheet, so there is no row to bonus. Per Ruling D the +2 has to hang on the thing it modifies — the persistent poison damage condition and its recovery roll — which means the sheet needs a marker attachable to a condition's own check, with the value inline, not a bonus on any stat.

proposed.clause: In addition, if you roll a success on a save against a disease or poison, you get a critical success instead.
proposed.freeText: A degree-of-success upgrade. It changes the result table for a whole class of saves and moves no number at all, so no bonus lane can express it. The sheet needs a per-check outcome-shift field carrying which check it applies to, which trigger scopes it (disease or poison), which degree is affected, and which direction it moves.

rows.name: Jotunborn Weapon Familiarity
rows.text: You gain access to all uncommon weapons with the jotunborn trait. You have familiarity with weapons with the jotunborn trait plus the bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear, and war flail—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.

proposed.clause: You have familiarity with weapons with the jotunborn trait plus the bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear, and war flail—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
proposed.freeText: Your weapon proficiency for a specific named set — every weapon with the jotunborn trait, plus bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear and war flail — must be computed one category down: martial ones use your simple-weapon rank, advanced ones use your martial rank. This changes the attack bonus shown for those weapons; it grants no rank increase of its own.

proposed.clause: You have familiarity with weapons with the jotunborn trait plus the bola, greataxe, halberd, maul, longspear, and war flail—for the purpose of proficiency, you treat any of these that are martial weapons as simple weapons and any that are advanced weapons as martial weapons.
proposed.freeText: Not a proficiency rank and not a bonus: a per-weapon CATEGORY override (martial read as simple, advanced read as martial) applied only when that weapon's proficiency is resolved, leaving the weapon martial/advanced for every other purpose. The affected set is defined two ways at once — dynamically by a trait (any weapon carrying the jotunborn trait, including ones that gain it later) and by an explicit six-name list — so the sheet needs trait-driven set membership unioned with a name list, feeding a downgrade rule at strike-proficiency lookup time.

rows.name: Clever Improviser
rows.text: You've learned how to handle situations when you're out of your depth. You gain the Untrained Improvisation general feat. In addition, you can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained, even if you are untrained.

proposed.clause: You gain the Untrained Improvisation general feat.
proposed.freeText: The named general feat Untrained Improvisation must be added to the character for free, with everything it in turn grants.

proposed.clause: you can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained, even if you are untrained.
proposed.freeText: The trained-proficiency gate on skill actions is lifted for this character: any skill action listed as requiring trained must still be reachable and shown as attemptable while untrained. No number changes, but the availability statement must be visible.

proposed.clause: you can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained, even if you are untrained
proposed.freeText: A permanent permission flag: skill actions that carry a trained-proficiency requirement must remain available to this character at untrained, so the sheet must not treat 'requires trained' as a bar for them.

proposed.clause: In addition, you can attempt skill actions that normally require you to be trained, even if you are untrained.
proposed.freeText: A global rules waiver with no number in it: it strips the trained-or-better requirement from every skill action that carries one. The sheet needs a character-level flag that changes action AVAILABILITY — trained-only skill actions must stop being filtered out or greyed out for this character — which no bonus lane can carry. A printed note is the floor; the actual requirement is that the gate itself is suppressed.

rows.name: Cornered Fury
rows.text: If a foe of a larger size than you critically hits and damages you, that foe is off-guard to you for 1 round.

rows.name: Experienced Professional
rows.text: You carefully safeguard your professional endeavors to prevent disaster. When you use Lore to Earn Income, if you roll a critical failure, you instead get a failure. If you're an expert in Lore, you gain twice as much income from a failed check to Earn Income, unless it was originally a critical failure.

proposed.clause: When you use Lore to Earn Income, if you roll a critical failure, you instead get a failure.
proposed.freeText: A conditional marker on the Lore skill entry (per Ruling C, on every Lore skill that could perform Earn Income) reading that a critical failure on an Earn Income check becomes a failure. Note that this is a degree-of-success adjustment, not a numeric bonus — no lane computes degrees of success, so what the sheet must be able to express is the conditional marker with the Earn Income trigger in its 'when', per Ruling D (the mark attaches to the action it modifies).

proposed.clause: If you're an expert in Lore, you gain twice as much income from a failed check to Earn Income, unless it was originally a critical failure.
proposed.freeText: A printable clause, gated on holding expert rank in Lore, that doubles the income from a failed Earn Income check (excluding an original critical failure). Nothing on the sheet computes downtime income, so the requirement is that the clause can be carried and shown conditionally against the Lore/Earn Income entry rather than that a number be recalculated.

proposed.clause: If you're an expert in Lore, you gain twice as much income from a failed check to Earn Income, unless it was originally a critical failure.
proposed.freeText: A second marker on the same Earn Income / Lore surface that only appears once the character's Lore proficiency reaches expert, stating that income from a failed check is doubled (excluding a result that was originally a critical failure). The gate is a proficiency-rank check on the specific Lore skill being used, and the payload is a downtime currency amount rather than a roll modifier.

proposed.clause: When you use Lore to Earn Income, if you roll a critical failure, you instead get a failure.
proposed.freeText: A degree-of-success reclassification bound to one activity and one skill family: a critical failure on a Lore check made to Earn Income is read as a failure instead. Nothing numeric changes — the result STEP of the roll is rewritten. It must attach to Earn Income under every Lore skill the character has (Ruling C's star-every-skill-that-could-perform-the-action shape), and it is not a bonus, so situational/passiveEffects cannot carry it.

proposed.clause: If you're an expert in Lore, you gain twice as much income from a failed check to Earn Income, unless it was originally a critical failure.
proposed.freeText: The Earn Income activity must be able to carry a rider that is gated on a proficiency RANK (expert in Lore), that multiplies the activity's payout on one specific degree of success (failure), and that carves out an exception for a failure which only became a failure via the previous clause — i.e. the rider has to know the roll's ORIGINAL degree, not just its final one. Ruling D settles where such a marker sits (on the action it modifies), but the sheet holds no income figure to double and no rank-gated marker text.

rows.name: Guerrilla Dedication
rows.text: You're skilled in subtle tactics and using the environment against your enemies. You become trained in your choice of Deception or Thievery; if you are already trained in both, you become an expert in one instead. When you take this dedication, choose a single, discrete urban or wilderness location, such as "Mzali" or "the Verduran Forest"; this becomes your favored location. When you are in this location and undetected by all enemies, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than half your Speed. During exploration, this also allows you to automatically approach within 15 feet of other creatures while Avoiding their Notice, as long as they aren't actively Searching or on guard. You can change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime in the new location you would like to set as your favored location.

proposed.clause: You become trained in your choice of Deception or Thievery
proposed.freeText: A player pick that grants the trained proficiency rank, with the pool restricted to exactly two named skills (Deception, Thievery) rather than any skill.

proposed.clause: if you are already trained in both, you become an expert in one instead
proposed.freeText: The already-trained fallback here does not redirect to a different skill: it must be able to yield the EXPERT rank in one of those same two skills, chosen by the player. So the sheet must express a conditional rank upgrade (trained -> expert) in Deception or Thievery that fires only when both are already trained.

proposed.clause: When you are in this location and undetected by all enemies, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than half your Speed.
proposed.freeText: A conditional marker on Stealth / the Sneak action stating that no Stealth check is rolled at all, gated on three printed conditions: being in your recorded favored location, being undetected by all enemies, and moving no more than half your Speed. It carries no number — the value it replaces is the roll itself. Whether you are standing in your favored location is unknowable to the sheet, so per Ruling M's shape the condition belongs in the marker's note rather than being modelled.

proposed.clause: choose a single, discrete urban or wilderness location, such as "Mzali" or "the Verduran Forest"; this becomes your favored location ... You can change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime
proposed.freeText: The sheet must record and display a player-authored favored location. Unlike a normal choice this has no enumerable option list — it is a free-text value the player types, and it must remain editable later (the feat allows changing it).

proposed.clause: When you take this dedication, choose a single, discrete urban or wilderness location, such as "Mzali" or "the Verduran Forest"; this becomes your favored location. … You can change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime in the new location.
proposed.freeText: No lane fits. The sheet must store a player-AUTHORED free-text value — the name of a favored location — captured when the feat is taken and editable afterwards. It is not a pick from an enumerable option list, so the standard choice lane's option-set shape does not describe it; there is no correct answer for the app to offer, only a text field the player fills in. The stored value is load-bearing because the feat's remaining clauses are gated on being in that named place.

proposed.clause: During exploration, this also allows you to automatically approach within 15 feet of other creatures while Avoiding their Notice, as long as they aren't actively Searching or on guard.
proposed.freeText: A second marker on the Avoid Notice activity (and the Stealth skill) with its own condition — in the favored location, targets not Searching and not on guard — stating the approach to 15 feet succeeds automatically. Distinct from the Sneak clause above: different action, different condition, so under the stacking ruling it is shown as its own entry rather than merged.

proposed.clause: choose a single, discrete urban or wilderness location, such as "Mzali" or "the Verduran Forest"; this becomes your favored location. … You can change your favored location by spending 1 week of downtime in the new location
proposed.freeText: A free-text, player-typed value stored on the character (the favored location) which the feat's own later clauses refer back to, and which must remain editable afterwards. It is not a pick from an enumerable option list — no game-data collection contains 'the Verduran Forest' as a selectable option — so the choice lane's named-option shape does not cover it.

proposed.clause: When you are in this location and undetected by all enemies, you can Sneak without attempting a Stealth check as long as you move no more than half your Speed.
proposed.freeText: A rider on the Sneak action that SUPPRESSES the roll entirely rather than modifying it — no Stealth check is attempted — under conditions the app can never verify (where you are standing, whether every enemy has you undetected, how far you moved this turn). Ruling M settles the surface (a permanent marker whose note carries the positional condition), but 'no roll is made' is not a bonus and has no numeric home; the sheet needs a way to say an action's check is waived.

rows.name: The Truth as I See it
rows.text: Your knack for spinning a believable reality from threads of story is so practiced that sometimes even you begin to believe what you're saying. When you use Deception to Lie, you can carefully structure your deceits so that each individual statement you make is the truth, from a certain perspective. Once per day when using Deception to Lie, you can roll twice and take the better result. This is a fortune effect. You don't take a penalty to Deception checks while subject to the ring of truth spell or similar effects. Whenever you are subject to ring of truth or a similar effect, you can attempt a Deception check when you first begin speaking to counteract the spell's effects, with a counteract rank equal to half your level (rounded up); succeeding at this check doesn't end the spell or effect, but it does cause it to indicate that you are speaking the truth, even when you are actually lying.

proposed.clause: Once per day when using Deception to Lie, you can roll twice and take the better result.
proposed.freeText: A once-per-day resource the sheet must track and let the player spend, refreshing on a day boundary.

proposed.clause: Once per day when using Deception to Lie, you can roll twice and take the better result. This is a fortune effect.
proposed.freeText: A conditional marker on the Deception skill, scoped to the Lie action, describing a roll-twice-take-higher fortune effect. It is a fortune effect, not a numeric bonus, so nothing adds into the Deception total — the requirement is that the marker can sit on Deception with the Lie trigger and the fortune tag in its note.

proposed.clause: You don't take a penalty to Deception checks while subject to the ring of truth spell or similar effects.
proposed.freeText: A conditional entry on Deception that suppresses the penalty ring of truth (or a similar effect) would impose, active only while you are subject to such an effect. The sheet must be able to express a negation of an external penalty rather than only additive bonuses.

proposed.clause: you can attempt a Deception check when you first begin speaking to counteract the spell's effects, with a counteract rank equal to half your level (rounded up)
proposed.freeText: No lane in the doc covers counteracting. The sheet must express a Deception-based counteract attempt whose counteract rank is a level-derived value — half your character level rounded up — recomputed as you level, shown against Deception with its trigger (being subject to ring of truth or similar). The follow-on wording ('doesn't end the spell but makes it indicate you are speaking the truth') is the outcome text that belongs with it.

proposed.clause: Whenever you are subject to ring of truth or a similar effect, you can attempt a Deception check when you first begin speaking to counteract the spell's effects, with a counteract rank equal to half your level (rounded up); succeeding doesn't end the spell but causes it to indicate you are speaking the truth.
proposed.freeText: A marker on Deception that must carry a DERIVED, level-scaling value: a counteract rank of ceil(character level / 2), recomputed as the character levels. That number is the load-bearing part — the rest (when it may be attempted, and that success does not end the effect) is prose for the note. If the app has no place to show a counteract rank on a skill check, this is the part with no home.

proposed.clause: Once per day when using Deception to Lie, you can roll twice and take the better result. This is a fortune effect.
proposed.freeText: Roll twice and keep the better result, scoped to one specific use of one specific skill (Deception to Lie). This changes how the die is RESOLVED rather than adding anything to it, and the fortune tag itself must be recorded so two fortune effects can be seen not to combine — there is no field for 'this roll is made twice' and none for the fortune/misfortune tag.

proposed.clause: You don't take a penalty to Deception checks while subject to the ring of truth spell or similar effects.
proposed.freeText: Cancellation of a penalty imposed by an OUTSIDE effect: the sheet never applied that penalty, so there is nothing to subtract from. What must be expressible is 'this named external effect's penalty does not apply to me' — a suppression keyed to a named spell plus an open-ended 'or similar effects' clause (Ruling H says stay open where the rules are open).

rows.name: Elemental Eyes
rows.text: You can see in the darkness as easily as an elemental. You gain darkvision. --- **Special** You can select this feat only at 1st level, and you can't retrain into or out of this feat.

proposed.clause: You gain darkvision.
proposed.freeText: Darkvision must appear on the senses row as a precise sense granted permanently by this feat.

rows.name: Shape of the Cloud Dragon
rows.text: You've discovered how to transform yourself into a cloud dragon. Once per day, you can cast 7th-rank Dragon Form as an innate arcane spell, transforming into a cloud dragon. The spell automatically heightens to 8th level if you're 16th level and 9th rank if you're 18th level. On a critical hit with an unarmed Strike gained from dragon form, you recharge the spell's breath weapon immediately. While in this form, you gain the following cloud dragon-specific abilities: - **Cloud** cloud walk (you can walk on clouds or fog); **Melee** 1 jaws, **Damage** 2d10 piercing plus 1d12 electricity; - **Melee** 1 claw (agile), **Damage** 3d10 slashing; - **Melee** 1 tail (reach 10 feet), **Damage** 3d10 bludgeoning; - **Melee** 1 horn (reach 10 feet), **Damage** 3d8 piercing; - Breath Weapon , 6d12 electricity. --- **Special** You can use this feat in place of Shape of the Dragon to fulfill feat requirements.

proposed.clause: Once per day, you can cast 7th-rank Dragon Form as an innate arcane spell, transforming into a cloud dragon.
proposed.freeText: Dragon Form must appear as a once-per-day innate spell of the arcane tradition, cast at rank 7, with its per-day use tracked. The text grants no spell attack or spell DC proficiency, so nothing else about spellcasting changes.

proposed.clause: The spell automatically heightens to 8th level if you're 16th level and 9th rank if you're 18th level.
proposed.freeText: The granted innate spell's rank is not fixed: it must be level-derived — rank 7 at levels 14-15, rank 8 at 16-17, rank 9 at 18+ — and re-evaluate as the character levels, since the form's numbers key off the rank cast.

proposed.clause: **Melee** 1 jaws, **Damage** 2d10 piercing plus 1d12 electricity; **Melee** 1 claw (agile), **Damage** 3d10 slashing; **Melee** 1 tail (reach 10 feet), **Damage** 3d10 bludgeoning; **Melee** 1 horn (reach 10 feet), **Damage** 3d8 piercing
proposed.freeText: Four form-specific unarmed strikes with exact damage dice and types (jaws 2d10 piercing plus 1d12 electricity; claw 3d10 slashing; tail 3d10 bludgeoning; horn 3d8 piercing), carrying their traits — agile on the claw, reach 10 feet on tail and horn. These replace your normal strikes and exist only while the cloud dragon form is active, so they must be scoped to that state rather than added permanently.

proposed.clause: While in this form, you gain the following cloud dragon-specific abilities: - **Cloud** cloud walk (you can walk on clouds or fog) ... - Breath Weapon , 6d12 electricity.
proposed.freeText: The cloud dragon form is an on/off state the sheet must be able to run, and it is the CLOUD dragon variant specifically, not generic Dragon Form: while active it grants cloud walk (movement over clouds or fog) and a Breath Weapon action dealing 6d12 electricity, alongside the form's strikes.

proposed.clause: On a critical hit with an unarmed Strike gained from dragon form, you recharge the spell's breath weapon immediately.
proposed.freeText: A clause printed against the form's strikes / the Breath Weapon action: a critical hit with a form-granted unarmed Strike immediately recharges the breath weapon, bypassing its normal recharge wait. Nothing here is a numeric bonus; the requirement is that the rider can be carried on the form's breath weapon entry.

proposed.clause: On a critical hit with an unarmed Strike gained from dragon form, you recharge the spell's breath weapon immediately.
proposed.freeText: A trigger that RESETS another ability's use limit: a critical hit with one of the form's Strikes refills the form's breath weapon, which otherwise waits out its own recharge. The resource being reset is not the character's — it exists only inside a temporary polymorph form granted by a spell — so the sheet needs a use counter that lives on a form, and a rule that refills it off a die result.

proposed.clause: Breath Weapon , 6d12 electricity
proposed.freeText: A named action the form grants, with its own damage expression (6d12 electricity) and its own recharge, existing only while the form is up.

proposed.clause: **Cloud** cloud walk (you can walk on clouds or fog)
proposed.freeText: A movement PERMISSION, not a speed: it adds no value and no new movement type, it makes an otherwise impossible surface traversable. The speed lane holds numbers for fly/swim/climb/burrow and has nothing that says 'this terrain is now walkable'.

proposed.clause: You can use this feat in place of Shape of the Dragon to fulfill feat requirements.
proposed.freeText: An equivalence consulted when OTHER records' prerequisites are checked: this feat must be able to declare that it counts as a differently-named feat. Reported because it rewrites the prerequisite graph for other records, not because this feat's own prerequisites matter.

rows.name: Lore Seeker
rows.text: You see what others don't, and you've developed magical tricks to find hidden truth. You can cast Translate, Sound Body, and See the Unseen as innate spells, each once per day. If you could already cast spells, these spells are of the same tradition. Otherwise, they are arcane spells, you use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability, and you become trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for arcane spells.

proposed.clause: You can cast Translate, Sound Body, and See the Unseen as innate spells, each once per day.
proposed.freeText: Three specifically named spells must appear on the sheet as innate spells, each with its own independent once-per-day use counter (three separate resources, not one shared use).

proposed.clause: If you could already cast spells, these spells are of the same tradition. Otherwise, they are arcane spells.
proposed.freeText: The tradition of those three innate spells is not a constant printed on the feat — it must be derived from the character: it inherits the tradition the character already casts in, and only falls back to arcane when the character has no other spellcasting.

proposed.clause: you become trained in spell attack rolls and spell DCs for arcane spells
proposed.freeText: Trained proficiency rank in arcane spell attack rolls and arcane spell DC, granted only on the branch where the character could not already cast spells.

proposed.clause: you use Intelligence as your spellcasting ability
proposed.freeText: For a character with no other spellcasting, the innate spells' statistics must be keyed to Intelligence. Nothing in the lane vocabulary names the key attribute of an innate-only spellcasting entry; without it there is no attribute modifier to build the spell attack roll and DC from.

rows.name: Marshal Dedication
rows.text: You've combined your social skills and combat training to become a talented combat leader. Choose Diplomacy or Intimidation. You become trained in that skill or become an expert if you were already trained in it. In addition, you're surrounded by a marshal's aura in a . Your aura has the emotion, mental, and visual traits and grants you and allies within the aura a +1 status bonus to saving throws against fear.

proposed.clause: you're surrounded by a marshal's aura ... grants you and allies within the aura a +1 status bonus to saving throws against fear
proposed.freeText: +1 status bonus to all three saving throws for the character themself, restricted to saves against fear effects. It is permanently active (you always occupy the centre of your own emanation), so the restriction belongs in the bonus's `when`, not in a toggle. The allies' half of the same sentence produces nothing on this sheet.

proposed.clause: Choose Diplomacy or Intimidation.
proposed.freeText: A pick made when the feat is taken, from a two-option named list (Diplomacy or Intimidation), recorded on the character.

proposed.clause: Choose Diplomacy or Intimidation. You become trained in that skill
proposed.freeText: A two-option pick between Diplomacy and Intimidation must be recorded on the sheet, and the picked skill's rank set to trained.

proposed.clause: or become an expert if you were already trained in it
proposed.freeText: If the chosen skill is already trained from any other source, the grant becomes expert in that same skill instead of trained — a conditional rank step, not a redirect to a different skill.

proposed.clause: You become trained in that skill or become an expert if you were already trained in it.
proposed.freeText: The chosen skill becomes trained; if the character was already trained in it, the grant is an upgrade to expert instead. The sheet must express a skill grant whose resulting rank depends on the rank the character already has.

proposed.clause: …grants you and allies within the aura a +1 status bonus to saving throws against fear.
proposed.freeText: A permanent +1 status bonus to the character's own saving throws against fear, restricted by wording to fear effects (and carrying the aura's positional condition in its note). The allies' share of the same bonus is deliberately nothing on this sheet.

proposed.clause: You become trained in that skill
proposed.freeText: Trained proficiency in whichever of the two skills was chosen.

proposed.clause: or become an expert if you were already trained in it
proposed.freeText: Rank escalation on redundancy: when the chosen skill is already trained, the grant becomes expert instead of being wasted or redirected. This is not 'choose a different skill' — the same skill goes up a rank, and the grant's rank therefore depends on the character's current rank in it.

rows.name: Divine Access
rows.text: Divine Access Source Advanced Player's Guide pg. 79 Your ability to tap into divine magic surpasses the spells traditionally available to you (the divine spell list). Choose one deity who grants one of your mystery's granted domains. Add up to three cleric spells of your choice granted by that deity to your spell list. You can select from these spells when you add or swap spells in your spell repertoire. Special You can select this feat more than once. You can't choose the same spells more than once, but you can choose a different domain or a different deity with the same domain you've previously selected with this feat.

proposed.clause: Choose one deity who grants one of your mystery's granted domains.
proposed.freeText: The sheet must store which deity was picked, with the option list filtered to deities granting a domain the character's mystery already grants.

proposed.clause: Add up to three cleric spells of your choice granted by that deity to your spell list.
proposed.freeText: Between one and three player-chosen spells, drawn from the picked deity's cleric spell list, are added to the character's own spell list so they become legal repertoire selections. Both the count (variable, up to three) and the individual spell picks must be stored.

proposed.clause: Special You can select this feat more than once. You can't choose the same spells more than once, but you can choose a different domain or a different deity with the same domain you've previously selected with this feat.
proposed.freeText: The feat must be takeable multiple times, with each taking storing its own deity and its own set of spell picks, and with spells already chosen by an earlier taking excluded from the later list.

proposed.clause: Special You can select this feat more than once. You can't choose the same spells more than once, but you can choose a different domain or a different deity with the same domain you've previously selected with this feat.
proposed.freeText: The feat is repeatable, so each instance must carry its own deity and its own set of spell picks rather than one shared record, and spells already taken by an earlier instance must be excluded from the later instance's options.

proposed.clause: Add up to three cleric spells of your choice granted by that deity to your spell list.
proposed.freeText: A second, dependent pick of up to three spells, whose option list is the cleric spells of the deity chosen in the previous clause. 'Up to three' means the count is variable, not fixed.

rows.name: Gunslinger Dedication
rows.text: You excel in using specific types of ranged weapons. You have familiarity with martial crossbows and firearms, treating them as simple weapons for the purposes of proficiency. You gain access to uncommon martial and simple crossbows and firearms that do not have an ancestry trait. You become trained in gunslinger class DC. Choose a gunslinger way. You become trained in your way's associated skill; if you were already trained in this skill, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You don't gain any other abilities from your choice of way.

proposed.clause: You have familiarity with martial crossbows and firearms, treating them as simple weapons for the purposes of proficiency.
proposed.freeText: Attack proficiency for every crossbow and firearm in the martial category must be computed from the character's simple-weapon rank instead of their martial rank. This is a category remap scoped to a named weapon subset, not a rank increase, so the sheet needs to express 'these specific weapons are treated as one category lower'.

proposed.clause: You become trained in gunslinger class DC.
proposed.freeText: A trained proficiency rank in the gunslinger class DC on a character who has no gunslinger class. The sheet needs a class-DC statistic that a non-class source can bring into existence and set a rank on. No lane in the manual covers class DC.

proposed.clause: if you were already trained in this skill, you become trained in a skill of your choice
proposed.freeText: When the way's associated skill is already trained from another source, the grant redirects to a free skill of the player's choice.

proposed.clause: You become trained in your way's associated skill
proposed.freeText: Trained rank in the one skill tied to the way that was picked; which skill it is is determined by that earlier choice rather than named on the feat.

proposed.clause: Choose a gunslinger way.
proposed.freeText: A way pick made when the feat is taken, from the gunslinger ways list, stored on the character because the next clause reads it.

proposed.clause: Choose a gunslinger way. ... You don't gain any other abilities from your choice of way.
proposed.freeText: The chosen way must be recorded, but purely as the input to the skill grant below — the text explicitly withholds every other benefit of that way, so selecting it must not pull in the way's deed, slinger's reload, or any other feature.

proposed.clause: You become trained in your way's associated skill
proposed.freeText: Trained proficiency in a skill determined by which way was chosen — the grant is looked up from the chosen option, not authored on the feat.

proposed.clause: You don't gain any other abilities from your choice of way.
proposed.freeText: The way must be recorded as a bare identity: the pick supplies the skill and nothing else, and must not confer the way's usual features (its deed, its slinger's reload, its critical specialization). A choice deliberately stripped of the grants that same choice normally carries.

rows.name: Critter Shape
rows.text: Once per hour, you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape. While in critter shape, you gain the effect of a 1st-rank Pest Form, except you can only transform into an animal matching your inherent animal. You can remain in critter shape for up to 10 minutes, after which you transform back into your hybrid shape and can't enter your critter shape again for 1 hour. You can instead use Change Shape to return to your humanoid or hybrid shape at any time during the duration of Critter Shape. If your inherent animal is normally larger than Tiny, you transform into a smaller, younger version of the animal, such as a Tiny bear cub. If your inherent animal has a fly Speed, you can turn into that animal (unlike normal for 1st-rank *pest form*), but you still don't gain a fly Speed.

proposed.clause: While in critter shape, you gain the effect of a 1st-rank Pest Form ... You can remain in critter shape for up to 10 minutes
proposed.freeText: A toggleable state, duration up to 10 minutes and dismissible early, that applies 1st-rank pest form's battle-form statistics to the character's own sheet: the form's AC, the form's attack modifier and damage for its unarmed attacks, its Speeds, and the suppression of the character's normal Strikes and manipulate actions.

proposed.clause: If your inherent animal has a fly Speed, you can turn into that animal (unlike normal for 1st-rank pest form), but you still don't gain a fly Speed.
proposed.freeText: Print beside the form: the form is restricted to the character's own inherent animal, and no fly Speed is gained even when that animal flies. The denial is explicit, so the state must not add a fly Speed.

proposed.clause: …you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape.
proposed.freeText: The Change Shape action the character already has gains an additional named form to enter — critter shape — so the option must appear on the existing action rather than as a standalone activity.

proposed.clause: Once per hour, you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape.
proposed.freeText: Adds a new form option to the Change Shape action the character already has from another record, rather than teaching a new named activity. The option must surface on that existing action.

proposed.clause: Once per hour ... you transform back into your hybrid shape and can't enter your critter shape again for 1 hour.
proposed.freeText: One use per hour, with the hour counted from when the form ends rather than when it starts — a per-hour resource with a cooldown, not a per-day pool.

proposed.clause: you transform into a smaller, younger version of the animal, such as a Tiny bear cub
proposed.freeText: While the state is active the character's size becomes Tiny, regardless of the size of the animal they are modelled on.

proposed.clause: Once per hour… You can remain in critter shape for up to 10 minutes, after which you transform back… and can't enter your critter shape again for 1 hour.
proposed.freeText: A per-hour resource the player spends: one entry per hour, a 10-minute cap on how long the shape lasts, and a 1-hour lockout before it can be entered again.

proposed.clause: Once per hour, you can use Change Shape to enter a critter shape.
proposed.freeText: A once-per-hour resource — an hourly period rather than the usual per-day one.

proposed.clause: except you can only transform into an animal matching your inherent animal
proposed.freeText: The form list is narrowed to a single animal determined by an earlier heritage selection (the character's inherent animal), so the state's options depend on another stored pick.

proposed.clause: You can remain in critter shape for up to 10 minutes, after which you transform back into your hybrid shape and can't enter your critter shape again for 1 hour.
proposed.freeText: The state carries a maximum duration (10 minutes) that ends it automatically, and the 1-hour lockout is measured from when the state ends rather than from when it began — a cooldown anchored to the end of a mode, not a use counted at its start.

rows.name: One Among The Masses
rows.text: It will take more than a gathered mass of foes to take you down. You gain resistance equal to your level to damage dealt by swarms, troops, and creatures who occupy the same space as you. In addition, you can briefly menace large groups of enemies to step aside. You gain the Overawe Crowd activity.

proposed.clause: You gain resistance equal to your level to damage dealt by swarms, troops, and creatures who occupy the same space as you.
proposed.freeText: A resistance entry whose value is the character's level (re-evaluated as they level, not a frozen number) and whose qualifier is the attacker — a swarm, a troop, or any creature sharing the character's space — rather than a damage type. The resistance row must be able to carry both a level-scaling value and an attacker-side condition.

proposed.clause: You gain the Overawe Crowd activity.
proposed.freeText: A named activity, Overawe Crowd, must appear in the character's list of actions. Only its existence is required; performing it is the player's job.

rows.name: Minor Omen
rows.text: **Frequency** once per day **Trigger** You fail a Reflex save. **Requirements** You can see the night sky. --- The stars warn you of danger in the nick of time. Reroll the failed save and use the new result.

proposed.clause: (the feat is a reaction: Trigger You fail a Reflex save)
proposed.freeText: The feat is itself a reaction, not a passive — the sheet must express its reaction action cost so it appears among the character's reactions rather than sitting inert in the feat list. (This is the record's own action cost, not a separately named activity, so grantsAction is a near-miss.)

proposed.clause: Reroll the failed save and use the new result.
proposed.freeText: A conditional, non-numeric marker on the Reflex save: once per day the character may reroll a failed Reflex save, while able to see the night sky. It moves no total — the sheet has to be able to hang a starred note on a save row that grants a reroll rather than a bonus.

proposed.clause: once per day … Reroll the failed save and use the new result.
proposed.freeText: One use per day that the player can spend and that resets on rest — the sheet must show whether Minor Omen is still available today.

proposed.clause: Reroll the failed save and use the new result.
proposed.freeText: The Reflex save row must be able to carry a reroll — a rule change, not a number. Nothing about the save's total changes; what the sheet needs is a place on the Reflex save to hang "once per day, if you fail, reroll and use the new result" (a forced-reroll / fortune effect), together with the once-per-day use so the player can see whether it is still available, and the "you can see the night sky" condition printed alongside it. No lane covers rerolling a roll: `situational` and `note` both assume a bonus or a printed remark, and this is neither.

rows.name: Wyrmling Flight
rows.text: Your draconic wings have grown large and strong enough for flight. You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed, using your wings to stay aloft.

proposed.clause: You gain a fly Speed equal to your Speed, using your wings to stay aloft.
proposed.freeText: A fly Speed must appear in the character's speeds, and its value must be DERIVED from the character's current land Speed rather than stored as a fixed number — it has to move when the land Speed moves (armour penalty, speed bonuses, later increases).

rows.name: Devout Blessing
rows.text: You gain the blessing of the devoted class feature, choosing from the listed blessings or any other to which you have access.

proposed.clause: You gain the blessing of the devoted class feature
proposed.freeText: The blessing of the devoted class feature must be granted to the character by this feat and appear on the sheet as an owned feature.

proposed.clause: choosing from the listed blessings or any other to which you have access
proposed.freeText: The feat must present a picker of blessings and record which one the player took; the option list is the printed blessings plus any others the character has access to.

proposed.clause: choosing from the listed blessings or any other to which you have access
proposed.freeText: Whatever the chosen blessing itself confers must flow through the pick onto the sheet — the choice cannot be a label only, the selected option has to carry its own grant.

rows.name: Advanced Targeting System
rows.text: Your ocular processors are augmented with advanced targeting systems, which allow you to more easily pinpoint your enemy and read their movements. You can cast Sure Strike once per day as a 1st-rank arcane innate spell.

proposed.clause: You can cast Sure Strike once per day as a 1st-rank arcane innate spell.
proposed.freeText: Sure Strike must appear on the spells page as an innate spell — tradition arcane, cast at 1st rank, with a once-per-day use that resets on daily preparation. The tradition and the rank are part of the requirement, not decoration: an innate spell entry that loses either is wrong.

rows.name: Unbowed, Unbroken
rows.text: Your connection to elemental wood manifests as resilience—towering trees, rough bark, deep roots, and patient determination. You gain the Unwavering Resilience reaction.

proposed.clause: You gain the Unwavering Resilience reaction.
proposed.freeText: A named activity, Unwavering Resilience, must be granted by this feat and appear in the character's actions with a reaction cost. Only its existence is required here — its internal effect belongs to that action's own record.

rows.name: Constant Levitation
rows.text: Your power has unbound you from the earth below. You're affected by a constant Fly spell, and when your Psyche is Unleashed, you gain a +10-foot status bonus to your fly Speed.

proposed.clause: You're affected by a constant Fly spell
proposed.freeText: A fly Speed must be present permanently on the sheet — always on, not a castable spell entry and not a limited-duration effect the player has to remember to switch on. Its value comes from Fly, i.e. equal to the character's current Speed, so it must track that number.

proposed.clause: when your Psyche is Unleashed, you gain a +10-foot status bonus to your fly Speed
proposed.freeText: The bonus must be gated to the already-existing Unleashed state (Unleash Psyche) — present only while that state is active, absent otherwise. This feat contributes a rider to a state another record owns.

proposed.clause: when your Psyche is Unleashed, you gain a +10-foot status bonus to your fly Speed
proposed.freeText: +10 feet, STATUS type, applied to the FLY Speed specifically — not to the land Speed and not to all speeds. The sheet must be able to aim a typed speed bonus at one non-land movement type.

rows.name: Quick Recognition
rows.text: You Recognize Spells swiftly. Once per round, you can Recognize a Spell using a skill in which you're a master as a free action.

proposed.clause: Once per round, you can Recognize a Spell using a skill in which you're a master as a free action.
proposed.freeText: The Recognize a Spell action must be able to carry a marker saying it can be taken as a free action, with the condition (the skill used must be master rank) in the note and a link back to this feat. Nothing on the sheet is computable from this — it is an action-cost change on an existing action, which per Ruling D marks the action itself.

proposed.clause: you can Recognize a Spell ... as a free action
proposed.freeText: The sheet must be able to attach a marker to the core skill action Recognize a Spell — an action this feat does NOT grant — stating that its action cost becomes a free action, once per round. This is an action-cost override on a pre-existing action, not a bonus and not a new action.

proposed.clause: using a skill in which you're a master
proposed.freeText: The override is gated on the character's proficiency rank in whichever skill performs the action: it applies only for skills the character is master or better in. The marker's condition therefore has to be evaluated per-skill against current rank (and per Ruling C, the plausible performing skills are Arcana/Nature/Occultism/Religion), not stated as a flat always-on property.

rows.name: Swimming Poppet
rows.text: Your fins, flippers, or other accessories assist with steering you through water. You gain a swim Speed of 15 feet.

proposed.clause: You gain a swim Speed of 15 feet.
proposed.freeText: The sheet must carry a swim Speed of 15 feet as a new movement type alongside land Speed.

rows.name: Blood and Spirit
rows.text: Your connection to the divine has sanctified your blood, but the power only manifests when you are shedding it. Choose holy or unholy. While you are taking persistent bleed damage, you can Interact to coat a piercing or slashing weapon you're wielding with your blood. Until the end of your turn, your Strikes with that weapon deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage with the chosen trait to creatures with the opposing trait. Alternatively, you can deal 1d6 damage to yourself (which can't be resisted in any way) as part of that Interact action if you aren't taking persistent bleed damage.

proposed.clause: Choose holy or unholy.
proposed.freeText: A two-option pick recorded on the character, made once. The stored answer must feed the damage rider below, because it sets both the trait attached to the extra damage and the opposing trait that gates it.

proposed.clause: While you are taking persistent bleed damage, you can Interact to coat a piercing or slashing weapon you're wielding with your blood. Until the end of your turn...
proposed.freeText: A toggleable state the player turns on for a single weapon and that runs until the end of the turn, so the strike rider below is live only while it is on. The printed precondition (you are taking persistent bleed damage, or you paid the self-damage instead) belongs in the mode's note.

proposed.clause: ...your Strikes with that weapon deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage with the chosen trait to creatures with the opposing trait.
proposed.freeText: While the state is on, Strikes with the coated weapon add 1d6 spirit damage carrying the chosen holy/unholy trait. Two conditions must be expressible: the rider is scoped to that one wielded piercing or slashing weapon, and it only lands against creatures with the trait opposing the one chosen.

proposed.clause: Until the end of your turn, your Strikes with that weapon deal an additional 1d6 spirit damage with the chosen trait to creatures with the opposing trait.
proposed.freeText: The player must be able to turn on a temporary state (switched on by the Interact that coats the weapon, lasting to the end of the turn) that adds 1d6 spirit damage carrying the chosen holy or unholy trait to Strikes with the one piercing or slashing weapon being wielded — with the restriction that it only lands on creatures of the opposing trait carried in its wording. The extra die is a rider on that weapon's Strike damage, not a flat bonus, and the damage trait must follow the holy/unholy pick.

proposed.clause: coat a piercing or slashing weapon you're wielding ... Strikes with that weapon
proposed.freeText: No lane covers this shape: the rider must bind to ONE specific wielded weapon instance chosen at the moment the state is switched on — not to a weapon group, trait, or every Strike — and that binding lasts only for the turn. The sheet needs a way for an activated state to name which inventory weapon it is riding on.

rows.name: Primal Dragonblood
rows.text: A dragon with a deep connection to the natural world, such as an adamantine dragon or a horned dragon, resides somewhere on your family tree. You tend to trust your instincts and might take on the role of a protector of the wilderness. You gain the trained proficiency rank in Nature. If you would automatically become trained in Nature (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice. You can use Nature to Sense Direction and Subsist in the wilds. If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose a primal dragon.

proposed.clause: You gain the trained proficiency rank in Nature.
proposed.freeText: Nature's proficiency rank must be set to trained by this feat.

proposed.clause: If you would automatically become trained in Nature (from your background or class, for example), you instead become trained in a skill of your choice.
proposed.freeText: When Nature training is already granted from another source, the grant must convert into a free choice of any other skill at trained — i.e. the fallback must detect the overlap and open a picker instead of silently wasting the grant.

proposed.clause: You can use Nature to Sense Direction and Subsist in the wilds.
proposed.freeText: Nature must be usable in place of Survival, scoped to the two named actions only (Sense Direction, and Subsist in the wilds) — not a blanket Nature-for-Survival swap.

proposed.clause: If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose a primal dragon.
proposed.freeText: A constraint on a DIFFERENT choice: the draconic-exemplar pick must be restricted to primal dragons, or at minimum carry a printed constraint on that picker. Nothing on the sheet computes from it; it narrows the legal options of another record's choice.

proposed.clause: If you choose a draconic exemplar, you must choose a primal dragon.
proposed.freeText: No lane fits: this record places a validity constraint on ANOTHER record's choice list — should the character ever pick a draconic exemplar, only primal dragons are legal options. It grants nothing and modifies nothing already granted; it filters a future pick made elsewhere.

rows.name: Domain Fluency
rows.text: You command a deep understanding of the domains related to your mystery. Choose one of the domains associated with your mystery for which you have an initial domain spell. You gain an advanced domain spell from that domain, which you cast as a revelation spell.

proposed.clause: Choose one of the domains associated with your mystery for which you have an initial domain spell.
proposed.freeText: A domain pick whose option list must be filtered twice: to domains associated with the character's mystery, and among those, only ones where the character already has the initial domain spell.

proposed.clause: You gain an advanced domain spell from that domain, which you cast as a revelation spell.
proposed.freeText: The advanced domain spell of the chosen domain must be added to the character's focus spells and presented as a revelation spell (oracle focus casting), with the spell's identity determined by the choice above — one grant per domain option rather than a single fixed spell.

proposed.clause: which you cast as a revelation spell
proposed.freeText: No lane covers this: the granted focus spell must be tagged as a REVELATION spell, not merely a focus spell, so it is treated by the oracle's revelation rules (cursebound escalation when cast) instead of as an ordinary focus spell. This is a category reclassification of a granted spell, not a modifier.

rows.name: Improbable Elixirs
rows.text: Your mastery of alchemical secrets enables you to replicate effects most believe can be achieved only via magic. Select a number of potions equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1); these potions must be of 9th level or lower.
